[textbook.md line 72~83]

Quantum mechanics is our main motivation for studying linear algebra, so we will use the standard notation of quantum mechanics for linear algebraic concepts.
The standard quantum mechanical notation for a vector in a vector space is the following:

$$
\begin{equation*}
|\psi\rangle . \tag{2.4}
\end{equation*}
$$

$\psi$ is a label for the vector (any label is valid, although we prefer to use simple labels like $\psi$ and $\varphi$).
The $|\cdot\rangle$ notation is used to indicate that the object is a vector.
The entire object $|\psi\rangle$ is sometimes called a ket, although we won't use that terminology often.
